answer: **Why ETFs can distribute fewer gains:** When an authorized participant redeems ETF shares, the fund can deliver low-basis securities in kind rather than selling them for cash. Under IRC §852(b)(6), a RIC recognizes no gain on that in-kind distribution, so it can purge its most appreciated lots without realizing gains. A cash-redeeming mutual fund must sell holdings, and those sales can generate capital gain distributions passed to all remaining shareholders. **Limits:** - The benefit applies only to in-kind redemptions. Cash creations and redemptions and rebalancing or index-change sales can still realize gains. - It depends on AP participation. Many bond and international ETFs rely more on cash. - Short-term gains still distribute as ordinary income. Dividends and interest are unaffected. - Your own sale of ETF shares is still taxable. The benefit avoids fund-level distributions, not tax altogether. - It requires RIC qualification, and the result is deferral, not permanent
original_answer:
**Why the ETF can distribute fewer gains:** When an authorized participant redeems ETF shares, the fund can hand over low-basis securities in kind instead of selling them for cash. Under IRC §852(b)(6), the RIC recognizes no gain on that in-kind distribution. The fund can therefore purge its most appreciated lots without realizing gains. A cash-dealing mutual fund must sell holdings to meet redemptions, and those sales can generate capital gain distributions that are passed to all remaining shareholders, including those who did not sell.

**Limits of the benefit:**
- It applies only to in-kind redemptions. Cash creations or redemptions, and rebalancing or index-change sales, can still realize gains.
- It depends on AP participation and creation/redemption activity. Some ETFs, such as many bond and international funds, rely more on cash.
- Short-term gains are still distributed as ordinary income, and dividends and interest are unaffected.
- Your own sale of ETF shares is still taxable, so the benefit is avoiding fund-level distributions, not eliminating tax.
- The fund must qualify as a RIC, and the result is deferral of gains rather than permanent exemption.
